items.readable_text:
Content:
Consider the function [MATH: f(x,y),] defined as

Content:
[MATH: f(x,y) = 2(x-1)^2(y-2).]

Content:
Let's determine the values of [MATH: x] and [MATH: y] for which the function is positive and negative.

Content:
As always, we first solve [MATH: f(x,y) = 0.] This gives

Content:
[MATH: 2(x − 1)^{2} ⋅ (y − 2) = 0|⟹2(x − 1)^{2} = 0or(y − 2) = 0.]

Content:
Solving these equations gives the solutions [MATH: x=1] and [MATH: y=2.] These solutions divide the [MATH: xy]-plane into four regions, as shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/b7a5ea37413569d0256fcd7b60e2707e]

Content:
We now determine the sign of [MATH: f(x,y)] in each region. To do this, we pick four test points, one for each region.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/8a50041cd21a0f663940cbc9021ebffe]

Content:
We compute the sign of [MATH: f(x,y)] in each region by calculating the sign at each test point. We record our results in a sign table.

Content:
| | Test point | [MATH: 2(x-1)^2] | [MATH: (y-2)] | [MATH: f(x,y) = 2(x-1)^2\cdot (y-2)] |
| Top-Left | [MATH: (0,3)] | [MATH: \color{blue}+] | [MATH: \color{blue}+] | [MATH: \color{blue}+] |
| Top-Right | [MATH: (2,3)] | [MATH: \color{blue}+] | [MATH: \color{blue}+] | [MATH: \color{blue}+] |
| Bottom-Left | [MATH: (0,1)] | [MATH: \color{blue}+] | [MATH: \color{red}-] | [MATH: \color{red}-] |
| Bottom-Right | [MATH: (2,1)] | [MATH: \color{blue}+] | [MATH: \color{red}-] | [MATH: \color{red}-] |

Content:
Using the last column of the table above, we get the following picture:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/fc090d930c1a09e260a5d4f9c759a8a9]

Content:
We can also record our findings using a simplified sign table, like the one below.

Content:
| [MATH: y > 2] | [MATH: \color{blue}+] | [MATH: \color{blue}+] |
| [MATH: y < 2] | [MATH: \color{red}-] | [MATH: \color{red}-] |
